text:
Turbidity within the Howard Creek Basin shows considerable temporal and spatial variations. Higher turbidity levels were recorded during 1973 sampling (Dysart, et al, 1973) than during the later studies of Iseman, et al. (1975). The highest values recorded were 165 JTU in West Bad Creek (July 26, 1973), 150 JTU at station H1 on Howard Creek (Sept. 9, 1975) and 175 JTU at station H7 also on Howard Creek (May 15, 1975). During June and July of 1973, high turbidity levels resulting from heavy rainfall were recorded in much of Howard Creek and in Bad Creek and West Bad Creek. Recorded values for Bad Creek and West Bad Creek were much higher than those measured at Limber Pole Creek and Corbin Creek during the same period, an indication of the recent land disturbances in the former areas.
Much of Howard Creek has suffered from siltation and sedimentation resulting from activities within the Howard Creek drainage. Past logging operations, road construction, explorations and core drilling from the proposed Bad Creek project, and use of logging roads by cross-county vehicles have all resulted in increased siltation in Howard Creek and its tributaries. The substrate of these streams contains large amounts of silt and fines, in some places measuring several feet in thickness.
Sediment investigations conducted in the Howard Creek Basin on particles of pebble size and smaller (Langdon, et al., 1976) show mean median particle size of basin sediments ranged from 0.180 - 0.578 mm, a size range classified as sand (Hough, 1957). The smaller particle sizes were, in general, found in Bad Creek, West Bad Creek, and the middle section of Howard Creek below the confluence with Bad and West Bad Creeks. The sediments were classified as "well-sorted," (a predominance of particles in a narrow range of sizes), with over 75 percent of the samples containing more fine (less than 0.5 mm in diameter) sediments than coarse (greater than 0.5 mm in diameter) sediments.
Erosion control measures were taken by the Applicant after exploratory drilling and excavations in the Bad Creek - West Bad Creek Basins, but in spite of these measures, some severe erosion occurred, adding to the problems in Howard Creek. The Applicant has since begun a program of erosion control to reduce siltation of local streams and preserve the land areas involved. As this program has only recently begun, it is not known whether the measures taken will be successful. Applicant's erosion control plan and recent measures taken are discussed in Section 4.
